title: Hermeticism today: from forged letters to TikTok
desc: Modern occult Hermeticism descends from a forged letter: Golden Dawn to tarot, Wicca and manifestation TikTok — and why scholars now study it all.
tldr: Nearly all modern Anglophone occultism descends from the Golden Dawn (1888) — an order chartered by letters that were almost certainly forged. From its milieu came the Rider–Waite–Smith tarot, Wicca and Thelema; from a parallel 1908 Chicago milieu came the 'seven principles' now circulating on TikTok. Meanwhile Hermeticism became a university discipline — which is exactly why there has never been a better time to read the sources.
body:
In March 1888, three London Freemasons consecrated the Isis-Urania Temple of the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn. Its charter rested on correspondence with a German Rosicrucian adept, Fräulein Anna Sprengel — correspondence that, as the historian Ellic Howe demonstrated in 1972, cannot be substantiated and was very probably fabricated by co-founder William Wynn Westcott. Hold that thought, because it is the axis of this whole step: the most influential document in modern occultism is one that never existed.

What the forgery built

The order it legitimated shaped nearly everything that now wears the word “Hermetic.” Its members included W.B. Yeats, Aleister Crowley, Florence Farr and A.E. Waite; unusually for the era, it admitted women on equal terms. After it fragmented around 1900, its published rituals became the source code of Anglophone occultism: Crowley’s Thelema grew out of its quarrels, Wicca out of its ceremonial vocabulary. Its single most influential artifact sits in millions of homes — the Rider–Waite–Smith tarot (1909), designed by Waite with the artist Pamela Colman Smith. The world’s default tarot imagery is Edwardian occultism, not ancient Egypt.

Two more names on the shelf

Franz Bardon (1909–1958), a Czech occultist who died in Communist custody, wrote what practitioners often rank as the century’s best magical training course — Initiation into Hermetics — a modern synthesis that engages the ancient Hermetica hardly at all. Manly P. Hall wrote his encyclopedic Secret Teachings of All Ages (1928) at twenty-seven, joined Freemasonry only in 1955, and received his honorary 33° in 1973 largely because of the book’s fame.

The algorithm’s Hermes

Today the word surfaces mostly as “the seven hermetic principles” in manifestation content. Those principles come from the Kybalion — 1908 Chicago New Thought, not antiquity — and the law-of-attraction lineage that quotes them is its sibling from the same milieu, which is why they “confirm” each other so smoothly. It would be easy to sneer, and wrong. The appetite is real: for a cosmos that means something, in which mind matters and the human being is not an accident. That is precisely the appetite Poimandres answered eighteen centuries earlier. The TikTok seeker and the Alexandrian student want the same thing; only the sources differ in quality.

The counter-movement: Hermes goes to university

While the popular literature multiplied, something quieter happened: the field professionalized. The University of Amsterdam founded its Centre for History of Hermetic Philosophy and Related Currents in 1999, with Wouter J. Hanegraaff in the chair; the European Society for the Study of Western Esotericism followed in 2005, with a peer-reviewed journal orbit. Sober information arrived decades after popular books had defined the terrain — but it has arrived, and much of it is free.

Why this is good news

So the map of “Hermeticism today” splits cleanly: a living occult reception with a forged birth certificate and genuine cultural force, and a young academic discipline finally doing the philology. Between them lies your opportunity. The critical texts exist, the scholarship is accessible, the distinctions are drawn. There has never — literally never, in five centuries of reception — been a better time to read the sources themselves. The final step hands you the map.

faq: Its founding documents include a probable forgery and its systems are modern syntheses — but it is a real, consequential religious current. Historians study it as modern religion, not as a survival of antiquity.
